page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates entry-level performance characteristics. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the average tier. However, multi-core and memory-intensive workloads show limitations. The Geekbench multi-core score of 1997.0 and Passmark CPU score of 1596.29 are positioned in the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached large-block read and write speeds registering at 26.99 GB/sec and 16.42 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-2 offers a resource-dense entry point into ARM64 development and testing without the overhead of x86 licensing. Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, such as static web serving, basic Redis caching, text processing, and ARM-native software compilation and testing. It is less suitable for memory-heavy databases, complex multi-threaded applications, or large-scale LLM inference.
